title: Trace and point classes on a regular proper curve over a separably closed field
statement: Let $k$ be a separably closed field [def-pc-separably-closed], let $D$ be a regular integral proper $k$-scheme of dimension $1$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], and let $\ell$ be prime, $n\geq1$ and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, with $\ell$ invertible in $k$. In ordinary small-etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] with Tate twists [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist], there is a canonical trace isomorphism $\operatorname{Tr}_{D/k}:H^2(D,\Lambda(1))\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda$. For every closed point $z\in D$, the enlargement of support of the regular Gysin class $\operatorname{Cl}_{z\hookrightarrow D}(1)$ has trace $[\kappa(z):k]$, where $\kappa(z)$ is the residue field [def-weil-residue-field] and the Gysin class is the one of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus].

source.place: Expose XVII §3.4.1, proof of Proposition 3.4.1.3, printed pp.271–272 (trace characterization of closed-point Gysin classes)

proof.text: Put $N=\ell^n$. The curve $D$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since proper includes finite type. A closed point $z$ has local dimension one: the generic point specializes to $z$, and there is no chain of two strict specializations in a dimension-one integral scheme. Thus $\mathcal O_{D,z}$ is a DVR by [lem-sc-regular-dim1-dvr]. Its maximal ideal is generated by a nonzerodivisor. This generator spreads to a neighbourhood: the ideal of $z$ is finite, and the quotient by the selected generator has zero stalk at $z$, hence vanishes after shrinking. Away from $z$ the ideal is the unit ideal. Therefore $z$ is an effective Cartier divisor. Its residue field is a finitely generated field algebra over $k$ on an affine neighbourhood, so $d_z=[\kappa(z):k]$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-lemma].

source.place: XVII 3.4.1.3, p.272: closed-point Gysin classes; elementary local-curve preparation

proof.text:
Choose an algebraic closure $K$ of $k$ and put $X=D_K$, $R=X_{\mathrm{red}}$, and $C=R^
u$ with its normalization map. The projection $X	o D$ is a universal homeomorphism by [det-curve-invariance-inseparable-closure]; hence $X$ has an irreducible nonempty underlying space of dimension one. By [rem-pc-regular-normal] $D$ is normal, and [lem-sc-normalization-over-normal-locus] identifies $D^
u$ with $D$. Consequently [lem-per-normalization-field-extension-homeomorphism] says that $C	o X$ is a universal homeomorphism. The reduction map $R	o X$ also is one by [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism]. Properness of $X$ follows from [lem-pc-degree-base-change] applied to $\mathcal O_D$; its closed reduction $R$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. Now [lem-sc-normalization-properties] gives that $C$ is a smooth proper connected curve of dimension one over the perfect field $K$, and that $
u:C	o R$ is birational. Write $u:C	o D$ for the composite.

source.place: XVII 3.4.1.3, p.272: expand the regular-curve trace input using Stacks 0C3N and normalization

proof.text: Use [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] to identify all inverse images of $\Lambda(1)$ with $\mu_N$ and the corresponding constant-coefficient twists. Pullback along $X\to D$ is an isomorphism on cohomology by [det-curve-invariance-inseparable-closure]. Pullback along $C\to X$ is an isomorphism by [thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance]. Composing gives the canonical $\Lambda$-linear isomorphism $\alpha=u^*:H^2(D,\Lambda(1))\xrightarrow{\sim}H^2(C,\mu_N)$.

source.place: XVII 3.4.1.3, p.272; Stacks 04DY/04DZ: ordinary etale topological invariance

proof.text: On $C$, [lem-sc-second-kummer-divisors] identifies $H^2(C,\mu_N)$ with $\operatorname{Pic}(C)/N$ by the Kummer boundary. The degree map on this quotient is an isomorphism by [det-cor-jacobian-torsion-pic]. Their composite is the degree-normalized trace $t_C$ of [def-wf-degree-normalized-curve-trace]. In particular $t_C(c_1(L))=\deg_K(L)\bmod N$ for every invertible module $L$ on $C$. This uses the smooth proper connected curve $C/K$, not the possibly nonreduced or nonsmooth curve $D_K$.

source.place: XVII 3.4.1.3, p.272, expanded by Milne Proposition 14.2 and Remark 14.6

proof.text:
Let $m$ be the multiplicity of the unique reduced component $R$ in $X$: $m=\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{X,\xi}}\mathcal O_{X,\xi}$. It is a finite positive integer by [lem-trf-degree-weighted-irreducible-components]. For any invertible module $L$ on $D$, the base-change clause of [lem-pc-degree-base-change], the single-component case of [lem-trf-degree-weighted-irreducible-components], and [lem-per-birational-curve-degree-invariance] applied to $C	o R$ give, in order,
$$\deg_k(L)=\deg_K(L|_X)=m\deg_K(L|_R)=m\deg_K(u^*L).$$
All curves in the degree formula are proper of dimension one. The hypothesis of [lem-per-birational-curve-degree-invariance] holds for $
u:C	o R$: by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-algebraic-normalization-field-change], applied to the reduced finite-type $K$-scheme $R$ with its single component, the normal locus $N\subseteq R$ is a dense open and $
u^{-1}(N)	o N$ is an isomorphism; $
u^{-1}(N)$ is a nonempty open, hence dense, subset of the integral scheme $C$. For $L=\mathcal O_D(z)$, the effective-divisor clause of [lem-pc-degree-base-change] gives $\deg_k(L)=\dim_k\kappa(z)=d_z$. Therefore, writing $a_z=\deg_K(u^*\mathcal O_D(z))$, one has the integer equality $m a_z=d_z$.

source.place: XVII 3.4.1.3, p.272; Stacks 0AYW, 0AYU and 0AYY: generic multiplicity and degree

proof.text: There exists a closed point $z_0$ of $D$ by [lem-sc-quasi-compact-kolmogorov-closed-point]: $D$ is a nonempty quasi-compact scheme, and its space is Kolmogorov: two points with the same closure would be two generic points of one irreducible closed subset, which [lem-sc-scheme-sober] forbids. By [lem-kun-sep-closed-finite-extension-purely-inseparable], each finite residue extension $\kappa(z)/k$ is purely inseparable. In characteristic zero it is trivial. In characteristic $p>0$, [lem-weil-pbc-purely-inseparable-pth-root-tower] expresses it as a finite tower of degree-$p$ extensions, so $d_z$ is a power of $p$. As $\ell$ is invertible in $k$, in either case $d_z$ is prime to $\ell$. The integer equality $m a_{z_0}=d_{z_0}$ of Step 5 then implies that both $m$ and $a_{z_0}$ are prime to $\ell$. They are therefore units in $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$.

source.place: XVII 3.4.1.3–3.4.1.4, p.272: invertibility of closed-point degrees

proof.text: Define $\operatorname{Tr}_{D/k}=m\,t_C\circ\alpha$. Both $t_C$ and $\alpha$ are isomorphisms by Steps 3–4; multiplication by $m$ is an automorphism by Step 6. Hence this is a $\Lambda$-linear isomorphism $H^2(D,\Lambda(1))\to\Lambda$.

source.place: XVII 3.4.1.3, p.272: construction with the required degree normalization

proof.text:
Let $b_z$ be the enlargement of support of $\operatorname{Cl}_{z\hookrightarrow D}(1)$. The codimension-one sign in [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] identifies $b_z$ with $+c_1(\mathcal O_D(z))$. The scheme-theoretic inverse image $u^*z$ is an effective Cartier divisor on $C$: a local equation for $z$ is nonzero at the generic point, remains nonzero under the dominant map $u$, and is a nonzerodivisor on the integral curve $C$. Its pulled-back ideal is consequently the Cartier ideal of $u^*z$, with $u^*\mathcal O_D(z)=\mathcal O_C(u^*z)$. Cartier-preserving pullback in [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer], including its equality after forgetting support, now gives $\alpha(b_z)=c_1(u^*\mathcal O_D(z))$. Thus Steps 4–5 give
$$\operatorname{Tr}_{D/k}(b_z)=m\,\deg_K(u^*\mathcal O_D(z))=d_z\quad\text{in }\Lambda.$$
The argument preserves the full scheme-theoretic divisor and its multiplicities; it never replaces $u^*z$ by its reduced point.

source.place: XVII 3.4.1.3, p.272: trace of the supported point class and the Kummer sign

proof.text: The value $d_{z_0}$ of Step 8 is a unit. Since the trace in Step 7 is an isomorphism, $b_{z_0}$ generates the cyclic $\Lambda$-module $H^2(D,\Lambda(1))$. Any $\Lambda$-linear map with the asserted point values is determined by its value $d_{z_0}$ on that generator. Hence the construction is independent of the chosen algebraic closure, of its presentation and of the auxiliary point, and is the canonical trace characterized in ILO XVII 3.4.1.3. This proves the isomorphism and the point-class formula simultaneously.

source.place: XVII 3.4.1.3, p.272: characterization of the trace

proof_origin.place: Expose XVII 3.4.1.3, printed p.272; its stated trace input expanded using Milne 14.2, 14.6 and the cited Stacks degree and normalization results.
